Most modern computers have internal temperature sensors on all important components, and will automatically power down a component that is getting too hot. There's also a large difference between too hot for a human to comfortably withstand, and too hot for a silicon chip to withstand. To put this in perspective, you'd likely be sweating around the neighborhood of 38C (100F), whereas the spec sheet for a modern CPU will typically list a max operating temperature of 105C (221F).

The thing to be wary of is that having a high ambient temperature in the room will diminish the effect of your computer's cooling systems. The heatsync in your computer is taking the heat from the chip and attempting to transfer this to the (relatively) cool air around the computer. The warmer the air is that you're trying to transfer heat to, the less heat it's actually going to take away from the chip. But remember, your chip will turn itself off if it goes above 105C. So just keep in mind that your computer will likely be running hotter than it could be by keeping it in a warm room, but if it's still running, you're still in the clear.

Also, keep a can of compressed air around and blow it out every so often. How often depends on the environment... For example, if you have pets that shed, or someone smokes in your household, you should dust more often (like once per month, nothing crazy). On the other hand, if you live in a hypo-allergenic bubble, you could probably get away with not dusting ;p
